html:
Marcus Furius Camillus was a Roman general and statesman of the early Roman Republic, who lived from about 446 to 365 BCE. Roman tradition made him a giant: dictator five times, the conqueror of Veii and the man who saved Rome from the Gauls.

The stories, told mainly by Livy, go like this. In 396 BCE he took Veii, the rich Etruscan city a few miles north of Rome, after a long siege. He was later sent into exile over the division of the spoils. When the Gauls beat Rome at the Allia and sacked the city (the Allia), he was recalled, drove them out and talked the Romans out of moving to Veii. For this he was called the second founder of Rome.

Modern historians doubt much of this. The rescue from the Gauls in particular looks like a later story to soften a humiliating defeat. But the capture of Veii was real, and it doubled the land Rome controlled.
